methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: The framing that Virginia's real challenge is small-business adoption rather than infrastructure signals a gap between data center buildout (concentrated, capital-intensive) and distributed capability development—businesses lack the fluency to leverage AI despite proximity to infrastructure.

signals.title: 3 or 4 data centers could be coming to a former coal mine site in Russell County
signals.signal_reading: Data centers coming to former coal sites in Russell County represents infrastructure concentration without evidence of local AI capability building—capital flows to Appalachia for power and land, not for distributed workforce development or deep technical adoption.

signals.title: Israeli AI maritime tech company joins Virginia Beach incubator - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Israeli maritime AI firm joining Virginia Beach incubator signals deep specialized capability clustering around defense/maritime sectors in Hampton Roads, reinforcing concentrated excellence in specific verticals rather than broad regional AI fluency.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: UVA students helping businesses explore AI represents peer-to-peer knowledge transfer mechanisms that could distribute practical AI capability beyond metro hubs—a potential pathway from concentrated academic expertise to distributed small-business adoption.

signals.title: Virginia Tech researcher weighs in on threats, fears of AI development - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech researcher commentary on AI development threats positions the university as a knowledge hub but signals expert concentration rather than broad regional capability—deep technical understanding remains siloed in academic institutions.
